high_value_lineage: Historical predecessor of proposal/evolution tooling: it separates generation from judging but still lets one model-produced verdict authorize a filesystem write.
Conceptual ancestor of later Ouroboros/Architect-gated evolution, but lacks a durable operator approval artifact.
Provides a concrete early form of generated-module provenance through ORIGIN filename headers.

concrete_findings.finding: Selected live-module source is sent wholesale to core.face.invoke without redaction or locality enforcement.
concrete_findings.risk: If face routes to an external provider, source code or embedded credentials may leave the machine.

concrete_findings.finding: LLM-generated code can be written directly into services/modules_live after only an LLM judge verdict and syntax parse.
concrete_findings.risk: Syntax-valid generated code may contain dangerous imports, destructive behavior, network exfiltration, privilege changes, persistence, or semantic regressions.

concrete_findings.finding: Generation and admission are not independently trusted.
concrete_findings.risk: The same model-facing infrastructure participates in both transmutation and judging; no deterministic benchmark or independent verifier is required.

concrete_findings.finding: Judge prompt exposes source/generated snippets and acceptance checks only whether APPROVED appears anywhere in the response.
concrete_findings.risk: Prompt injection or ambiguous model output can become an approval.

concrete_findings.finding: Processed state is keyed only by basename.
concrete_findings.risk: Same-named modules in different subdirectories collide.

concrete_findings.finding: Materialized output is also named from basename and written into the target root.
concrete_findings.risk: Different source paths sharing a basename can overwrite the same alien_rex_<basename> artifact.

concrete_findings.finding: alien_memory.json is overwritten directly and non-atomically with broad exception suppression on load.
concrete_findings.risk: Crash/corruption can lose or silently reset change-tracking state.

concrete_findings.finding: Runtime sleeps 60 seconds while comment says 10 minutes.
concrete_findings.risk: Actual model-call cadence can be 10x more frequent than the operator expects.

concrete_findings.finding: No source-size/token/cost bound exists before full-code transmutation.
concrete_findings.risk: Large module selection can cause unexpectedly large model requests, latency, or cost.

concrete_findings.finding: Existing alien_rex_<basename> is overwritten without append-only artifact identity or exact predecessor binding.
concrete_findings.risk: Evolution history can be lost and generated lineage cannot be deterministically replayed.

required_gates: No raw live source may leave the host unless an explicit provider/data-egress policy permits it.
Canonical source identity must be relative-path + exact SHA-256, never basename alone.
Generated output must be stored as immutable proposal artifact outside modules_live.
Never overwrite an existing proposal; use content-addressed identity and append-only lineage.
Static gate must inspect imports/effect surfaces in addition to syntax.
Run unit/integration/regression tests in an isolated environment before any admission.
Use deterministic or independently measured performance/correctness criteria; LLM opinion alone cannot establish superiority.
Generation verdict and admission authority must be separated.
Human/Architect or typed policy approval must be represented by a durable approval receipt.
Live activation must be a separate explicit action and default-deny.
Atomic state writes with fsync/rename or durable ledger semantics.
Bound source bytes, model tokens, frequency and concurrent requests.
Redact or block credential-shaped material before any permitted external model request.
Pin model/provider/prompt/version/hash in provenance if a model participates in proposal generation.

lineage_links.relationship_to_current_architecture: Historical predecessor candidate for proposal-only evolution / Ouroboros / Architect-gated admission.
